html:
Since the fall of Gaddafi in 2011, Libya has been the main point of departure for migrants from Africa trying to cross the Mediterranean to Italy, many in unsafe boats run by smugglers.

Migrants from West Africa, the Horn and beyond cross the Sahara to the Libyan coast. There many are held in detention centres or by armed groups, where beatings, forced labour and ransom are common. In 2017 footage of migrants being sold at auction near Tripoli shocked the world.

Thousands have drowned at sea. The European migrant crisis led the European Union and Italy to pay the Libyan coast guard to stop the boats, a policy much criticised. See also the second civil war and the old Saharan routes.
sum: Since the fall of Gaddafi in 2011, Libya has been the main point of departure for migrants from Africa trying to cross the Mediterranean to Italy, many in unsafe boats run by smugglers.
